occurrences.original_stem: A primitive structure that develops into auricle of left atrium?
occurrences.explanation: The primitive atrium forms the trabeculated atrial regions and auricles.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following will develop heart?
occurrences.explanation: Cardiogenic mesoderm is the visceral (splanchnic) layer of lateral plate mesoderm.

occurrences.original_stem: The rough part of the left ventricle develops from:
occurrences.explanation: The primitive ventricle forms the trabeculated left ventricle.

occurrences.original_stem: The vascular system develops at:
occurrences.explanation: Cardiovascular development begins in the third embryonic week.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following primitive vessels contributed to the development of the heart?
occurrences.explanation: The right common cardinal vein contributes to the superior vena cava. The original broad stem is ambiguous because the left common cardinal vein also contributes to cardiac venous structures.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following helps with the development of the left auricle?
occurrences.explanation: The primitive atrium forms the auricles; pulmonary veins contribute to the smooth left atrial wall.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is the primitive structure of the coronary sinus?

original_options.A: Left sinus horn of sinus venosus
original_options.B: Right sinus horn of sinus venosus

occurrences.explanation: The left horn of the sinus venosus gives rise to the coronary sinus.

occurrences.original_stem: A newborn has a defective coronary sinus, and the cause is most likely congenital. Which part of the primitive heart tube is most likely responsible for the defect?
occurrences.explanation: The coronary sinus is a derivative of the left sinus horn.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following primitive structures develops into the left auricle?
occurrences.explanation: Both auricles arise from the primitive atrium.

occurrences.original_stem: The vestibule of the left ventricle is formed from?
occurrences.explanation: The conus cordis, part of the bulbus cordis, forms the smooth ventricular outflow regions.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient has a thin outflow part of the right atrium. What is the most likely defect?
occurrences.explanation: The body and right horn of the sinus venosus contribute to the smooth posterior right atrial wall. This is an inflow region; the original outflow wording was incorrect.

occurrences.original_stem: After birth, the patent ductus arteriosis is an abdominal connection between:

original_options.A: Arch of aorta and pulmonary trunk

occurrences.explanation: The ductus connects the proximal descending aorta near the aortic isthmus to the pulmonary artery. It is not an abdominal connection.

occurrences.original_stem: ostium secundum is a defect in:

original_options.D: Lower part of septum secundum ( ) ﻞﺤﻨﺗﻢﮭﻔﻟﺎﺑﺲﺑﺎﺼﻧةرﻮﻛﺬﻣﻮﻣ

occurrences.explanation: The normal ostium secundum develops by resorption in the superior septum primum; a secundum ASD is a separate pathological concept.

occurrences.original_stem: with potent ductus arteriosis the blood :

original_options.A: Moves from pulmonary trunk to aortic arch
original_options.B: Moves from pulmonary trunk to ascending aortic
original_options.C: Moves from umbilical vein to SVC
original_options.D: Moves from umbilical artery to placenta

occurrences.explanation: Fetal ductal flow is predominantly from pulmonary artery to descending aorta; after birth uncomplicated PDA usually shunts in the opposite direction.

occurrences.original_stem: which of the following is not included in the tetralogy of Fallot?
occurrences.explanation: The four defining abnormalities are VSD, overriding aorta, right ventricular outflow obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient was found to have their aorta originating from the right ventricle and the pulmonary arteries originating from the left. What is the name of this defect?
occurrences.explanation: In transposition, the aorta arises from the right ventricle and pulmonary trunk from the left ventricle.

occurrences.original_stem: defect in the heart that cause overrides both ventricles and receives blood from both sides what is the reason?
occurrences.explanation: Failure of outflow tract septation produces a common arterial trunk receiving blood from both ventricles; an overriding aorta alone does not uniquely identify this mechanism.

occurrences.original_stem: what structure can cause Atrial septal defects (ASD) through the opening of?
occurrences.explanation: Failure of postnatal fusion of septum primum and septum secundum leaves a patent foramen ovale. PFO and a true atrial septal tissue defect should not be conflated.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following embryonic structures allows fetal blood to circulate from the pulmonary trunk to the descending aorta before birth?
occurrences.explanation: The ductus arteriosus permits fetal pulmonary arterial blood to bypass the lungs.

occurrences.original_stem: A child presents to the ER, and after a series of procedures, you determine that his aorta is on the right side of his pulmonary trunk. What is the cause behind this defect?

original_options.A: Failure of conotruncal septum to follow its spiral course
original_options.C: Failure of conotruncal ridges to fuse

occurrences.explanation: Failure of the aorticopulmonary septum to spiral is the classic embryological explanation for transposition. Arterial origins must be established; rightward position alone is insufficient.

occurrences.original_stem: Pulmonary stenosis, VSD, overriding aorta, and ventricular hypertrophy are characteristic of which of the following?
occurrences.explanation: This combination identifies tetralogy of Fallot; the hypertrophy is specifically right ventricular.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient has ventricles that share one outflow tract. What is the most likely defect?
occurrences.explanation: Persistent truncus arteriosus is a single arterial outflow serving both ventricles; failure of septation is its mechanism.

occurrences.original_stem: Failure of the conotruncal ridge to twist results in which condition?
occurrences.explanation: Nonspiraling outflow septation leads to transposition of the great arteries.

occurrences.original_stem: Which embryonic structure closes to form the ligamentum teres?
occurrences.explanation: The obliterated left umbilical vein becomes the ligamentum teres hepatis.

occurrences.original_stem: The imaging technique used to follow up a patient with aortic valve stenosis is:
occurrences.explanation: Echocardiography assesses valve anatomy, transvalvular flow and stenosis severity.

occurrences.original_stem: A newly born baby is born cyanotic and having difficulty breathing. On examination, a well-heard diastolic murmur suggests valvular stenosis. The imaging technique used is:
occurrences.explanation: Echocardiography is the initial structural assessment for suspected congenital heart disease and valve lesions; the original murmur timing alone does not localize a valve.

occurrences.original_stem: What view of the heart does lead II, III, and , AVF represent?
occurrences.explanation: Leads II, III and aVF view the inferior myocardial surface.

occurrences.original_stem: Lead 2 is :

original_options.A: +ve in Right arm and -ve in left arm
original_options.B: +ve in Right arm and -ve in left leg
original_options.C: +ve in Left leg and -ve in Right arm
original_options.D: +ve in Left leg and -ve in Left arm

occurrences.explanation: Lead II records left leg positive relative to right arm negative.

occurrences.original_stem: What wave in the ECG represents repolarization of both ventricles?
occurrences.explanation: The T wave reflects ventricular repolarization.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is correct regarding the electrical impulse that generates from the SA node as seen on an ECG?
occurrences.explanation: The PR interval is measured from P-wave onset to QRS onset and normally lasts 0.12–0.20 seconds. SA node discharge itself is not visible on the surface ECG.

occurrences.original_stem: What wave in the ECG represents ventricular repolarization?
occurrences.explanation: Ventricular repolarization produces the T wave.

occurrences.original_stem: The ventricle becomes completely depolarized in ECG accompanied with the plateau in which of the following phases ?
occurrences.explanation: The ST segment corresponds broadly to the ventricular action-potential plateau.

occurrences.original_stem: Ventricular repolarization in ECG is represented by?
occurrences.explanation: The T wave represents ventricular repolarization.

occurrences.original_stem: In a healthy heart, the QRS waves correspond to?
occurrences.explanation: The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient has an elevated ST segment and inverted T wave. What is the likely diagnosis?
occurrences.explanation: Territorial ST elevation with an ischemic presentation suggests acute myocardial infarction, but ECG changes require clinical correlation.

occurrences.original_stem: What indicates QRS in ECG?
occurrences.explanation: QRS represents electrical depolarization of the ventricles.

occurrences.original_stem: ST elevated in the ECG indicates that the patient has ?
occurrences.explanation: New territorial ST elevation with ischemic symptoms is concerning for STEMI; isolated ST elevation also has noninfarction causes.

occurrences.original_stem: What does the ECG show ?

original_options.A: The ECG shows elevated S-T segment
original_options.B: The ECG shows elevated T wave
original_options.C: The ECG shows prolonged P-R interval
original_options.D: The ESG shows inverted S-T segment

occurrences.explanation: The pictured ST segment is above its baseline. This identifies an ECG finding, not a definitive diagnosis.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient was given an ACE inhibitor and developed arrhythmia. What is the most likely ion imbalance causing this, given that a tall, peaked T- wave is visible on the ECG?
occurrences.explanation: ACE inhibition reduces aldosterone and can cause hyperkalemia, whose ECG changes include peaked T waves.

occurrences.original_stem: In first-degree heart block what can be expected ?

original_options.A: PR interval is less than 0.12 ( 3 small squares)
original_options.C: P wave is sometimes followed by QRS
original_options.D: P wave is not followed by QRS

occurrences.explanation: First-degree AV block prolongs PR beyond 0.20 seconds while every P wave still conducts.

occurrences.original_stem: What make Narrow and tall peaked T wave in ECG?
occurrences.explanation: Tall, narrow, tented T waves are classically associated with hyperkalemia.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient is noted to have an abnormally shortened PR interval on their ECG. What could be the cause?
occurrences.explanation: WPW pre-excitation classically produces a short PR, a delta wave and a widened QRS; short PR alone is not diagnostic.

occurrences.original_stem: What is the cause of the ecg in the picture above?
occurrences.explanation: The supplied tracing shows a tall peaked T wave, the classic pattern in hyperkalemia.

occurrences.original_stem: An ECG shows no P-waves and an irregular rhythm. What does this represent?
occurrences.explanation: Absent discrete P waves and an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm suggest atrial fibrillation.

occurrences.original_stem: In ECG tall Peaked T-wave with “tent” like appearance indicates?
occurrences.explanation: A tented T wave is a classic hyperkalemia clue.

occurrences.original_stem: Which ECG shows ventricular extrasystole?
occurrences.explanation: Option C shows a premature broad ventricular complex and a subsequent pause.

occurrences.original_stem: Which one of the pairing statements is correct?

original_options.A: First heart sound - closure of semilunar valves
original_options.C: Isovolumetric relaxation phase - sharp decrease in ventricular pressure
original_options.D: Right Atrial systole - passive filling of the ventricle

occurrences.explanation: Ventricular pressure falls quickly during isovolumetric relaxation while the volume remains unchanged.

occurrences.original_stem: What will happen at the beginning of the isovolumetric contraction?
occurrences.explanation: AV valve closure begins ventricular isovolumetric contraction.

occurrences.original_stem: Regarding Ventricular Systole?

original_options.B: Ends by the end of plateau
original_options.C: Corresponds P wave in the ECG

occurrences.explanation: Ventricular contraction requires intracellular calcium binding to troponin C. Mechanical systole persists beyond the plateau; the source answer B is wrong.

occurrences.original_stem: When the ventricular pressure is lower than the atrial pressure this leads to:
occurrences.explanation: AV valves open when atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure.

occurrences.original_stem: Between AV valves closure and opening of Semilunar valves is the following phase:
occurrences.explanation: Between AV closure and semilunar opening, ventricular pressure rises with no change in volume.

occurrences.original_stem: The lowest ventricular volume occurs during which phase?
occurrences.explanation: End-systolic volume persists throughout isovolumetric relaxation.

occurrences.original_stem: QRS complex of ECG occurs immediately before which phase?
occurrences.explanation: Ventricular depolarization immediately precedes the onset of isovolumetric contraction.

occurrences.original_stem: Which line represents the Isovolumetric relaxation phase ?
occurrences.explanation: The diagram labels isovolumetric relaxation D to A, its left descending limb.

occurrences.original_stem: At which point the closing of the mitral valve will occur ?
occurrences.explanation: In this diagram B is the lower-right point at end-diastolic volume, where the mitral valve closes.

occurrences.original_stem: Which line represents the isovolumetric relaxation phase in the pressure-volume loop of the left ventricle?
occurrences.explanation: D to A is the constant-volume pressure fall after aortic valve closure.

occurrences.original_stem: In the ejection phase, the atrioventricular valves ......,and the semilunar valves...... .
occurrences.explanation: During ejection, AV valves are closed and semilunar valves are open.

occurrences.original_stem: The phase of the cardiac cycle between mitral valve closure and aortic valve opening?
occurrences.explanation: Mitral closure to aortic opening defines isovolumetric contraction.

occurrences.original_stem: Point A represents?
occurrences.explanation: This particular diagram places A at the lower-right corner: mitral valve closure.

occurrences.original_stem: On cardiac examination, the patient’s rhythm was normal with S4 at the apex. What characterizes the S4 sound?

original_options.A: It is caused by atrial relaxation during ventricular ejection
original_options.B: It can be heard in patients with left ventricular hypertrophy
original_options.C: It can be heard with stethoscope in the diaphragm
original_options.D: It has a high frequency, usually 600 cycles/sec

occurrences.explanation: S4 may occur when atrial contraction fills a stiff hypertrophied ventricle. It is a low-frequency sound best heard with the bell.

occurrences.original_stem: At which point does the mitral valve closure occur?
occurrences.explanation: In this diagram B, the lower-right corner, marks mitral valve closure.

occurrences.original_stem: The graph shows ventricle pressure-volume relationship; point A is:
occurrences.explanation: No independent diagram is supplied. The immediately preceding diagram labels A at mitral opening, conflicting with the printed answer. Merge with the verified Q13 or hold this item out of scored testing.

occurrences.original_stem: Reduced ejection fraction occurs in which of the following ?
occurrences.explanation: Reduced ejection fraction indicates impaired systolic pump function.

occurrences.original_stem: If there was an infarction of the AV node that caused an abnormal increase in the AV nodal delay, what will this affect?
occurrences.explanation: Physiological AV nodal delay permits atrial emptying before ventricular contraction. Excessive pathological delay can disturb atrioventricular coordination.

occurrences.original_stem: Arteries are elastic and recoil during diastole, why?
occurrences.explanation: Elastic arterial recoil sustains forward flow during diastole; it also helps maintain diastolic pressure, making the original A and B both defensible.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is not a classic ECG change in MI:

original_options.D: Abnormal development of deep Q wave

occurrences.explanation: A double or bifid P wave is an atrial abnormality; ST changes, T inversion and pathological Q waves can occur with infarction.

occurrences.original_stem: The red line in the figure separate ARP from RRP which statement is correct?

original_options.B: ARP in cardiac muscle is longer than skeletal muscle
original_options.C: During ARP can case premature impulse

occurrences.explanation: The cardiac refractory period is prolonged by the ventricular action-potential plateau; no propagated premature action potential can be triggered during the absolute refractory period.

occurrences.original_stem: What wave in the ECG represents repolarization?
occurrences.explanation: The T wave represents ventricular repolarization.

occurrences.original_stem: Resistance to blood flow?
occurrences.explanation: Arterioles are the principal adjustable resistance vessels.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is correct regarding to the electric impulse that generates from the SA node in ECG?
occurrences.explanation: Normal PR duration is 0.12–0.20 seconds; the SA node signal itself is not a visible surface ECG wave.

occurrences.original_stem: What increases the force of cardiac contractility?
occurrences.explanation: Digitalis increases available intracellular calcium by inhibiting Na+/K+-ATPase and thereby enhances ventricular contractility.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient is noted to have an abnormally shortened PR interval on their ECG, What could he have?
occurrences.explanation: The intended option is WPW: an accessory pathway can cause pre-excitation and shortened PR.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is NOT a classic change in ECG in myocardial infarction?

original_options.C: Development of an abnormal Q wave

occurrences.explanation: A bifid P wave is not a classic infarction change.

occurrences.original_stem: Which line represents the isovolumetric relaxation phase?
occurrences.explanation: The depicted D–A limb is isovolumetric relaxation.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient was found to have their aorta originating from the right ventricle and the pulmonary arteries originating from the left. What is the name of this defect?
occurrences.explanation: These arterial origins define transposition of the great arteries.

occurrences.original_stem: Inflammation is the current favorites hypothesis for atherosclerosis. Which of the following diagnostic marker would be indicative of increased inflammation?
occurrences.explanation: C-reactive protein is a marker of systemic inflammation; high-sensitivity CRP can inform cardiovascular risk.

occurrences.original_stem: What disease is LDL a risk factor for?
occurrences.explanation: Elevated LDL promotes atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; the intended answer should specify coronary heart disease.

occurrences.original_stem: case A man presents with aortic aneurysm and a palpable abdominal mass what’s the pathogenesis ?
occurrences.explanation: Fibrofatty intimal plaques identify atherosclerosis, commonly associated with AAA. AAA pathogenesis itself involves inflammation and medial extracellular-matrix degradation, so the original causal wording oversimplifies the disease.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following primitive vessels shared in the development of the heart?
occurrences.explanation: The right common cardinal vein helps form the SVC. The original stem was nonspecific because left common cardinal derivatives include the coronary sinus.

occurrences.original_stem: Blood pressure is described as:

original_options.B: Stroke volume times heart rate divided by total peripheral resistance
original_options.D: Cardiac output divided by stroke volume

occurrences.explanation: MAP is approximately cardiac output multiplied by systemic vascular resistance when right atrial pressure is negligible.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following helps with development of the left auricle?
occurrences.explanation: The primitive atrium gives rise to the auricles.

occurrences.original_stem: AV nodal cells have?

original_options.A: The lowest firing potential in the cardiac conduction system

occurrences.explanation: AV nodal pacemaker cells have spontaneous diastolic depolarization and lack a stable resting membrane potential. Their conduction is slow.

occurrences.original_stem: Total peripheral resistance (TPR) mainly depends on?
occurrences.explanation: Arteriolar radius is the principal adjustable determinant of systemic resistance; resistance varies inversely with the fourth power of radius.

occurrences.original_stem: Blood pressure increase and heart rate decrease due response to:
occurrences.explanation: Raised intracranial pressure can cause hypertension with reflex bradycardia, part of the Cushing response.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is a vasoconstrictor?
occurrences.explanation: Endothelin-1 contracts vascular smooth muscle; NO, prostacyclin and EDHF promote vasodilation.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is associated with primary (essential) hypertension?
occurrences.explanation: Established essential hypertension commonly involves increased systemic arteriolar resistance; renal, neurogenic tumor and endocrine causes are secondary.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with hypertension was stable on a drug but later required another drug that caused fatigue and sexual dysfunction. The new drug is most likely:
occurrences.explanation: Beta blockade may cause fatigue and sexual dysfunction.

occurrences.original_stem: A woman has a family history of hypertension, consumes a high-salt diet, and has a sedentary lifestyle. Her hypertension does not improve by drugs alone. Why?

original_options.A: Environmental factors amplify her genetic susceptibility
original_options.B: Her blood volume is always decreased
original_options.C: Her sympathetic activity is completely absent

occurrences.explanation: Salt intake and inactivity interact with polygenic susceptibility; lifestyle measures remain important alongside drugs.

occurrences.original_stem: What does the QRS complex represent on an ECG?
occurrences.explanation: QRS represents ventricular depolarization; ventricular repolarization forms the T wave.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with heart failure and hypertension is on hydralazine. Which drug combination is most appropriate to control the condition?
occurrences.explanation: Hydralazine can provoke reflex tachycardia and sodium retention; a beta blocker and diuretic counter these effects. This is the conventional hydralazine combination, not a complete modern heart failure regimen.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient has regurgitation due to damage to a structure of the heart valve. Which structure is most likely affected?
occurrences.explanation: Chordal rupture causes prolapse/flail of an AV valve leaflet and regurgitation. Papillary muscle injury can also cause regurgitation, so the generic stem does not uniquely distinguish them.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following are common primary sites of cancer that can metastasize to the heart?
occurrences.explanation: Lung and breast cancers commonly metastasize to the heart, particularly the pericardium.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with hypertension was stable on a drug but later required another drug that caused fatigue and sexual dysfunction. The new drug is most likely:
occurrences.explanation: Fatigue and sexual dysfunction are recognized beta blocker adverse effects.

occurrences.original_stem: A 50-year-old man has controlled hypertension. An ECG shows a premature ventricular complex. Which of the following is the diagnosis?
occurrences.explanation: The stem directly states the diagnosis. A useful version would describe an early wide QRS without a preceding P wave, usually followed by a compensatory pause.

occurrences.original_stem: A short QT interval is associated with:
occurrences.explanation: Hypercalcemia shortens the ST segment and therefore the QT interval.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient presents with nodules on his feet. Which infectious agent is associated with this condition?
occurrences.explanation: HHV-8 causes Kaposi sarcoma, which can form violaceous nodules on the feet. Nodules alone are nonspecific.

occurrences.original_stem: After birth, the patent ductus arteriosis is an abdominal connection between:

original_options.A: Arch of aorta and pulmonary trunk

occurrences.explanation: The ductus joins the left pulmonary artery near its origin to the proximal descending aorta just distal to the left subclavian artery.

occurrences.original_stem: ostium secundum is a defect in:
occurrences.explanation: The ostium secundum forms through resorption in the upper septum primum. A secundum ASD may result from excessive resorption or inadequate septum secundum development.

occurrences.original_stem: Which one of the pairing statements is correct?

original_options.A: first heart sound - closure of semilunar valves
original_options.C: iso-volumetric relaxation phase - sharp decrease in ventricular pressure
original_options.D: Right Atrial systole - passive filling of the ventricle

occurrences.explanation: All valves are closed while ventricular pressure falls without a volume change.

occurrences.original_stem: hypertension can be age related. A rising in systolic pressure can be considered a part of normal aging process. Why does systolic pressure increase?
occurrences.explanation: Arterial stiffness reduces aortic compliance, raising systolic and pulse pressure with aging.

occurrences.original_stem: The rough part of the left ventricle develops from:
occurrences.explanation: The primitive ventricle gives rise to the trabeculated left ventricle.

occurrences.original_stem: What will happen at the beginning of the isovolumetric contraction?
occurrences.explanation: Ventricular pressure exceeding atrial pressure closes AV valves, initiating isovolumetric contraction.

occurrences.original_stem: When the ventricle pressure is lower than in atrial pressure this leads to:
occurrences.explanation: When ventricular pressure falls below atrial pressure, AV valves open and filling begins.

occurrences.original_stem: the mechanism of action of digitalis :

original_options.D: increases The slope of SA node

occurrences.explanation: Digitalis inhibits the sodium-potassium pump; intracellular sodium rises, reducing calcium extrusion through Na+/Ca2+ exchange and increasing contractility.

occurrences.original_stem: with potent ductus arteriosis the blood:

original_options.A: moves from pulmonary trunk to aortic arch
original_options.B: moves from pulmonary trunk to ascending aortic
original_options.C: moves from umbilical vein to SVC
original_options.D: moves from umbilical artery to placenta

occurrences.explanation: Fetal ductal flow is pulmonary artery to aorta. A usual postnatal PDA shunts from aorta to pulmonary artery; the supplied answer reverses this.

occurrences.original_stem: Point A represents?
occurrences.explanation: In this figure point A is the lower-right corner at end-diastolic volume; mitral closure precedes the vertical isovolumetric contraction limb.

occurrences.original_stem: Decrease force of ventricular contraction occurs in
occurrences.explanation: L-type calcium channel blockade reduces myocardial calcium entry and contractility, particularly with verapamil or diltiazem.

occurrences.original_stem: What view of the heart does lead II, III, and , AVF represent?
occurrences.explanation: Leads II, III and aVF view the inferior surface.

occurrences.original_stem: ECG with no P-waves and irregular rhythm represents:
occurrences.explanation: AF typically shows no discrete P waves and an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm.

occurrences.original_stem: What drug is contraindicated in a hypertensive patient with arterial renal stenosis?
occurrences.explanation: ACE inhibition can markedly reduce GFR in bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a solitary functioning kidney. Unilateral stenosis is not an automatic contraindication.

occurrences.original_stem: which of the following is not included in the tetralogy of Fallot?
occurrences.explanation: Tetralogy of Fallot comprises VSD, RV outflow obstruction, overriding aorta and RV hypertrophy; ASD is not one of the four.

occurrences.original_stem: Patient with blood pressure of 240/130 what is the expected microscopic change in the arterioles?

original_options.A: Deposition of homogeneous plasma protein material
original_options.B: Concentric proliferation of smooth muscle cell

occurrences.explanation: Severe accelerated hypertension can cause hyperplastic onion-skin arteriolosclerosis; fibrinoid necrosis may coexist.

occurrences.original_stem: In ECG tall Peaked T-wave with “tent” like appearance indicates:
occurrences.explanation: Hyperkalemia classically causes narrow, tall peaked T waves.

occurrences.original_stem: 12 years old boy developed beta-hemolytic streptococcus pharyngitis which resolved spontaneously, however three weeks later he presented with a skin rush and his doctor hear murmur on physical examination, which of the following changes is least likely to be found in the heart of this boy at this stage of his disease?

original_options.B: Fibrosis of the mitral valve with fusion of the commissures
original_options.C: Foci of fibrinoid necrosis in mitral valve

occurrences.explanation: Acute rheumatic carditis can show Aschoff bodies, valvular fibrinoid injury and fibrinous pericarditis; scarring and commissural fusion are chronic sequelae.

occurrences.original_stem: What is the nature of anitschow cells ?
occurrences.explanation: Anitschkow cells are activated macrophages with characteristic caterpillar-like chromatin in rheumatic Aschoff bodies.

occurrences.original_stem: year old woman ... blood cultures are positive for gram positive bacteria. Urine analysis show hematuria. An ecg shows a 1.5 cm vegetation on the mitral valve. Which of the following conditions is this patient most likely to develop?
occurrences.explanation: Left-sided infective endocarditis can send septic emboli into systemic arteries and cause cerebral infected aneurysms. Hematuria may reflect immune-complex glomerulonephritis.

occurrences.original_stem: At birth, a patent ductus arteriosus is an abnormal connection between:
occurrences.explanation: Persistent ductus arteriosus connects the pulmonary circulation to the proximal descending aorta.

occurrences.original_stem: A 71-year-old woman has had a 10-kg weight loss accompanied by severe nausea and vomiting of blood for the past 8 months. On physical examination, she is afebrile. Biopsy specimens obtained by upper gastrointestinal endoscopy show adenocarcinoma of the stomach. Which of the following cardiac lesions is most likely to be present in this woman?
occurrences.explanation: Advanced adenocarcinoma can promote a hypercoagulable state with sterile platelet-fibrin vegetations.

occurrences.original_stem: 30 years old patient known that he have HIV infection for several years. Complained of rapidly spread Multiple red-purple skin plaques and nodules. Whats the virus associated with this case?
occurrences.explanation: HHV-8 is the etiologic agent of Kaposi sarcoma; HIV-associated immunosuppression favors disseminated lesions.

occurrences.original_stem: Case about Patient have temporal headache, Whats the vascular disease?
occurrences.explanation: New temporal headache in an older adult, especially with jaw claudication or visual symptoms, suggests giant cell arteritis.

occurrences.original_stem: Reduced ejection fraction in which of the following ?
occurrences.explanation: Reduced contractility lowers stroke volume relative to end-diastolic volume, reducing ejection fraction.

occurrences.original_stem: A female has controlled hypertension for months which of the following is LEAST likely to occur?
occurrences.explanation: Hypertension is strongly associated with atherosclerosis and myocardial infarction. Monckeberg medial calcification is a distinct process that usually does not narrow the lumen.

occurrences.original_stem: Case: a patient with heart murmur, what is the least expected finding?
occurrences.explanation: A murmur does not establish acute versus chronic rheumatic disease. Aschoff bodies and fibrinous pericarditis can occur acutely, while fused scarred valves suggest chronic disease.

occurrences.original_stem: On cardiac examination, the patient's rhythm was normal with S4 at the apex. What characterizes the S4 sound?

original_options.A: it's caused by atrial relaxation during ventricular ejection
original_options.B: it can be heard in patients with left ventricular hypertrophy
original_options.C: it can heard with the stethoscope diaphragm
original_options.D: it has a high frequency, usually 600cycles/ sec

occurrences.explanation: Atrial contraction into a stiff ventricle produces a low-frequency late-diastolic S4, best heard with the bell at the apex.

occurrences.original_stem: At which point does the mitral valve closure occur?
occurrences.explanation: In the provided loop B is the lower-right corner at end-diastole: mitral closure starts isovolumetric contraction.

occurrences.original_stem: Patient came to the hospital and the doctor diagnosed with heart failure but the doctor didn’t request ECG because?

original_options.A: ECG is not diagnostic of heart failure

occurrences.explanation: ECG does not by itself confirm HF; echocardiography assesses structure/function. Nevertheless ECG is normally part of the initial HF workup, so the stated reason for omitting it is misleading.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following primitive structure develops into left auricle ?
occurrences.explanation: The trabeculated portions and auricles of both atria arise from the primitive atrium.

occurrences.original_stem: 70 years old man have pulsating palpable abdominal mass he has hypertension and controlled by antihypertensive drug and he is heavy smoker for 40 years what is the pathogenesis of his condition?

original_options.A: Weakening of the blood vessels due to atherosclerosis
original_options.B: Weakening of the blood vessels do to cystic media

occurrences.explanation: A smoker with a pulsatile abdominal mass likely has an abdominal aortic aneurysm, associated with atherosclerosis, inflammation and medial extracellular matrix destruction.

occurrences.original_stem: What wave in the ECG represents ventricular repolarization?
occurrences.explanation: T waves represent ventricular repolarization.

occurrences.original_stem: defect in the heart that cause overrides both ventricles and receives blood from both sides what is the reason?

occurrences.original_stem: in the ECG, the diagnosis of heart block is confirmed if:
occurrences.explanation: A PR interval over 200 ms with 1:1 AV conduction defines first-degree AV block. Other blocks require different findings; the generic statement is too broad.

occurrences.original_stem: Ventricular extra systole is followed by:
occurrences.explanation: A PVC typically does not reset the SA node, so the next sinus impulse remains scheduled; interpolated PVCs and retrograde resetting are exceptions.

occurrences.original_stem: Tall T-wave in ECG are suggested of:

occurrences.original_stem: in the ECG, the diagnosis of heart block is confirmed if:
occurrences.explanation: First-degree AV block has PR >200 ms with all atrial impulses conducted; this does not define every type of heart block.

occurrences.original_stem: Ventricular extra systole is followed by:
occurrences.explanation: A PVC commonly leaves sinus timing unchanged, producing a full compensatory pause.

occurrences.original_stem: Tall T-wave in ECG are suggested of:
occurrences.explanation: Hyperkalemia classically produces tall narrow peaked T waves.

occurrences.original_stem: Analysis of ECG can identify:
occurrences.explanation: ECG can reveal ischemic ST-segment and T-wave abnormalities.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following events is represented by the ECG?
occurrences.explanation: P waves represent atrial depolarization. Atrial repolarization is also electrical activity present on the ECG but usually hidden in QRS; SA and AV nodal depolarization are not directly discernible.

occurrences.original_stem: During the isovolumetric relaxation phase:
occurrences.explanation: Relaxation lowers ventricular pressure without changing volume until AV valves open.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following events is represented by the ECG?
occurrences.explanation: A P wave represents atrial depolarization, while atrial repolarization usually occurs during the QRS. The ECG in general represents multiple electrical events.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is a component of the DASH diet?
occurrences.explanation: DASH emphasizes fruit, vegetables and low-fat dairy, and sodium restriction is recommended to help lower blood pressure.

occurrences.original_stem: A 40-year-old heavy smoker with long-standing hypertension (180/100 mmHg), chronic cough and difficulty breathing requires an antihypertensive. Which option is most appropriate?
occurrences.explanation: Smoking and chronic respiratory symptoms do not distinguish these two usual antihypertensive choices. BP 180/100 generally warrants combination treatment, and albuminuria, kidney function or other comorbidities would affect choice.

occurrences.original_stem: Which is a modifiable factor in primary hypertension?
occurrences.explanation: Dietary salt, excess weight and physical inactivity are modifiable; age, heredity and ethnicity are not.

occurrences.original_stem: Blood regurgitates backward into an atrium. Damage to which structure may be responsible?
occurrences.explanation: Chordal rupture disrupts AV leaflet support, allowing systolic regurgitation into an atrium.

occurrences.original_stem: A 45-year-old patient has multiple red-blue vascular nodules on the face, containing dilated blood-filled vessels and dystrophic calcification. What is the most likely diagnosis?
occurrences.explanation: Large dilated blood-filled vascular spaces with thrombosis and calcified phleboliths favor a cavernous vascular lesion.

occurrences.original_stem: Which vasculitis affects the aorta and its major branches?
occurrences.explanation: Takayasu is a large-vessel granulomatous vasculitis of the aorta and its major branches.

occurrences.original_stem: Which is included in the pathogenesis of primary hypertension?
occurrences.explanation: Impaired natriuresis can sustain volume expansion and contribute to essential hypertension; renal or adrenal diseases are secondary causes.

occurrences.original_stem: What stimulates the release of atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP)?
occurrences.explanation: Increased atrial filling stretches atrial myocytes and stimulates ANP release, promoting natriuresis and vasodilation.

occurrences.original_stem: Which factor contraindicates a renin–angiotensin– aldosterone system-blocking antihypertensive drug?
occurrences.explanation: ACE inhibitors, ARBs and direct renin inhibitors can injure the fetal kidneys and are avoided in pregnancy.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient reports chronic visual symptoms and has retinal exudates. Which assessment is appropriate?
occurrences.explanation: Hypertensive retinopathy can cause hemorrhages and exudates; BP assessment is appropriate, although retinal exudates have other causes.

occurrences.original_stem: An athlete has increased inhibitory vagal tone affecting the SA node action potential. Which phase becomes prolonged?
occurrences.explanation: Vagal M2 signaling reduces pacemaker slope and hyperpolarizes SA nodal cells, delaying threshold and lengthening phase 4.

occurrences.original_stem: Which is a function of vascular endothelium?
occurrences.explanation: Activated or injured endothelium can promote clot formation, while healthy endothelium is predominantly antithrombotic. Calling clot formation its unqualified function is incomplete.

occurrences.original_stem: Which can cause left ventricular hypertrophy?
occurrences.explanation: Elevated systemic pressure increases LV afterload and causes concentric hypertrophy. The preload distractor is incomplete; chronic preload overload can also cause eccentric hypertrophy.

occurrences.original_stem: Which antihypertensive drug is given by IV infusion in a hypertensive crisis?

original_options.A: Sodium nitroprusside [Other options were not provided.]

occurrences.explanation: Nitroprusside is an IV arterial and venous vasodilator that can lower pressure rapidly in selected hypertensive emergencies under close monitoring; other IV agents are often used depending on the emergency.

occurrences.original_stem: Maximum left ventricular volume occurs during:
occurrences.explanation: LV volume is at end-diastolic maximum throughout isovolumetric contraction, until aortic opening begins ejection.

occurrences.original_stem: Maximum coronary blood flow occurs during:
occurrences.explanation: Left coronary flow rises sharply as systolic myocardial compression is released during early ventricular relaxation. This statement primarily concerns the left coronary circulation.

occurrences.original_stem: Girl 16 years old did take drug that caused hypertension and Abolished by Saralasin , what is the drug?
occurrences.explanation: Saralasin is an angiotensin receptor peptide antagonist; it blocks the pressor action of angiotensin II.

occurrences.original_stem: A newborn has a defective coronary sinus, and the cause was mostly congenital, which part of the primitive heart tube is the most likely cause of the defect ?
occurrences.explanation: The left sinus horn contributes the coronary sinus and oblique vein of the left atrium.

occurrences.original_stem: From which primitive structure the left auricle arises form?
occurrences.explanation: The left auricle comes from the primitive atrium; incorporated pulmonary veins form the smooth left atrial wall.

occurrences.original_stem: A defect in the ostium secundum is a defect in which of the following?
occurrences.explanation: The ostium secundum forms in the superior septum primum by resorption. Secundum ASD can also result from poor septum secundum development.

occurrences.original_stem: Pulmonary stenosis, VSD, overriding aorta and ventricular hypertrophy presentation is characteristic of which of the following ?
occurrences.explanation: The four defining findings are RV outflow obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta and RV hypertrophy.

occurrences.original_stem: Male diabetic patient has peripheral vessel disease as he has hypertension.What is contraindicated in this case ?
occurrences.explanation: Diabetes and peripheral arterial disease alone do not absolutely contraindicate all beta blockers. Caution concerns peripheral symptoms and masking adrenergic hypoglycemia warnings, particularly with nonselective agents.

occurrences.original_stem: ventricular repolarization in ECG is represented by:

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with hypertension and diabetes after several weeks, he became less aware of hypoglycaemia. Which drug is the most likely used ?
occurrences.explanation: Beta blockade can blunt adrenergic warning symptoms of hypoglycemia, such as tachycardia. Sweating may remain present.

occurrences.original_stem: increasing radius by 2 fold, decreases the peripheral resistance by what ?
occurrences.explanation: Poiseuille resistance varies inversely with radius to the fourth power, so doubling radius makes resistance 1/16 as large, assuming other variables remain constant.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with hyperthyroidism, which drug mechanism is given to manage cardiovascular problem?
occurrences.explanation: Beta blockers reduce adrenergic tachycardia and palpitations in hyperthyroidism; high-dose propranolol also reduces peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion.

occurrences.original_stem: Its embryonic origin is:

original_options.D: Atrial systole with rapid flow of blood from atria to ventricle

occurrences.explanation: Saralasin blocks angiotensin II receptors, preventing an angiotensin-mediated pressor response.

occurrences.original_stem: If injected nicotine intravenously into an anesthetized cat, which of the following effect would be expected?

original_options.D: Hypertensive effect that is antagonized by phentolamine

occurrences.explanation: Aortic stenosis causes left ventricular pressure overload and concentric hypertrophy, conditional on the lesion being aortic stenosis.

occurrences.explanation: Ventricular depolarization (QRS) immediately precedes ventricular isovolumetric contraction.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is part of the anatomy of the atrioventricular valves?

occurrences.original_stem: A patient lost 300ml of blood after a hemorrhage, what is the most likely physiological response?
occurrences.explanation: Blood loss reduces circulating volume, venous return and central venous pressure. Reflex tachycardia may compensate; increased cardiac output is not the expected primary response.

occurrences.original_stem: Someone has rib scoliosis; from your understanding, how will this affect his hemodynamic mechanism?

original_options.B: Decreased venous return due to decreased thoracic widening in inspiration
original_options.C: Increased venous return due to increased thoracic widening in inspiration

occurrences.original_stem: A patient has the ventricles sharing one outflow tract, what is the most likely defect?
occurrences.explanation: Failure of conotruncal/aorticopulmonary septation produces persistent truncus arteriosus, a single common arterial outlet.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient has a thin outflow part of the right atrium, most likely defect?
occurrences.explanation: The smooth sinus venarum of the right atrium derives from the right sinus horn; the trabeculated body derives from primitive atrium. The phrase “thin outflow part” and combined option A are malformed.

occurrences.original_stem: vestibule of left ventricle is formed of ?
occurrences.explanation: The conus cordis portion of the bulbus cordis forms the smooth ventricular outflow tracts, including the aortic vestibule.

occurrences.original_stem: Failure of the conotruncal ridge twisting?
occurrences.explanation: Failure of the aorticopulmonary septum to spiral is associated with transposition of the great arteries.

occurrences.original_stem: The phase of the cardiac cycle between mitral valve closure and aortic valve opening?
occurrences.explanation: During isovolumetric contraction, both mitral and aortic valves are closed while ventricular pressure rises.

occurrences.original_stem: Which point represents mitral valve closure? A B C D
occurrences.explanation: Point B is the lower-right corner of the supplied pressure-volume loop: mitral closure at end-diastolic volume.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with low arterial blood pressure, what is the reflex?
occurrences.explanation: Reduced arterial pressure reduces carotid baroreceptor stretch and firing, increasing sympathetic and reducing vagal outflow.

occurrences.original_stem: A person with a headache has hypertension. What compensatory response is initiated ?
occurrences.explanation: Increased blood pressure activates the arterial baroreceptor reflex, which buffers the rise in pressure.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient's biopsy of the small blood vessels revealed pink homogenous hyaline tissue, most likely cause?
occurrences.explanation: Hyaline arteriolosclerosis is associated with chronic hypertension and diabetes; malignant hypertension favors hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis and fibrinoid necrosis.

occurrences.original_stem: The following shows what complication? PICTURE

occurrences.original_stem: A patient came with excruciating chest pain to the ER, he died, and their biopsy showed the descending thoracic aorta of normal caliber had ruptured, found a blood filled space in the middle layer of the blood vessel, most likely cause of death?
occurrences.explanation: An intimal tear permits blood to dissect through the aortic media; rupture can occur without preexisting aneurysmal dilation.

occurrences.original_stem: What is a predisposing factor to heart failure?
occurrences.explanation: Acute myocardial infarction can reduce myocardial pumping function and precipitate heart failure.

occurrences.original_stem: Patient has an abdominal palpable pulse, most likely cause?
occurrences.explanation: An expansile pulsatile abdominal mass suggests abdominal aortic aneurysm; pulsation alone is not diagnostic.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient came to the ER with chest pain, they have a history of uncontrolled hypertension, they died, most likely cause of death?
occurrences.explanation: Necrosis is the intended irreversible myocardial injury, but chest pain and hypertension alone do not establish MI or the cause of death.

occurrences.original_stem: Patient came in with acute Ml and died, the most likely cause of death?
occurrences.explanation: Sudden early death after acute MI is frequently caused by malignant ventricular arrhythmias.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is stage 2 hypertension?
occurrences.explanation: 180/100 mmHg meets stage 2 hypertension under the ACC/AHA classification; stage 2 begins at 140 systolic or 90 diastolic.

occurrences.original_stem: A diabetic patient came in with masked hypoglycemia symptoms after starting a drug, this drug is most likely?
occurrences.explanation: Beta blockers such as atenolol can mask adrenergic warning signs of hypoglycemia, especially tachycardia.

occurrences.original_stem: A diabetic patient came in with chest pain, they also have intermitent claudication (peripheral vascular disease), which drug is contraindicated for this patient?
occurrences.explanation: Peripheral arterial disease and diabetes are not blanket contraindications to beta blockers. Selection depends on indication, selectivity, severity and other comorbidities; the source B is outdated as a general claim.

occurrences.original_stem: ACEI's and ARBs share similar adverse reactions, but what do only ACEI's cause?
occurrences.explanation: ACE inhibitors increase bradykinin and can cause dry cough; ARBs are much less likely to do so. Both can cause hypotension and hyperkalemia.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient was given an ACEl and got arrhythmia problems, what it the most likely ion imbalance cause (not 100% sure of how right the question is here????) a tall peaked t-wave was visible on ECG
occurrences.explanation: ACE inhibition reduces aldosterone, which can cause hyperkalemia; peaked T waves and potentially fatal arrhythmias may result.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient was given two doses of adenosine but still the ___ remains, what is the best drug to give?

occurrences.explanation: For stable regular narrow-complex SVT persisting after adenosine, an IV beta blocker or diltiazem/verapamil may be appropriate. Instability requires synchronized cardioversion; avoid AV nodal blockers in preexcited AF. The source omits rhythm and stability.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient is on an anti-anginal drug but took a holiday and forgot his medication, this would be disastrous if the drug was most likely?
occurrences.explanation: Abrupt clonidine withdrawal can cause rebound sympathetic activation and severe hypertension, but clonidine is an antihypertensive, not a usual antianginal. If the stem truly asks antianginal withdrawal, a beta blocker is also relevant.

occurrences.original_stem: Mechanism of action of aspirin?
occurrences.explanation: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates cyclooxygenase, reducing platelet thromboxane A2 production.

occurrences.original_stem: Which drug will decrease the sympathetic response and renin secretion?
occurrences.explanation: Beta blockers inhibit cardiac sympathetic effects and beta-1-mediated renin release from juxtaglomerular cells.

occurrences.original_stem: Which is a primary cause of hypertension?
occurrences.explanation: Impaired renal sodium excretion contributes to primary hypertension; chronic kidney disease and renal tumors are potential secondary causes. Primary hypertension is multifactorial.

occurrences.original_stem: Decrease sodium retention helps with hypotension how?
occurrences.explanation: Reduced sodium retention lowers extracellular fluid and plasma volume, helping lower blood pressure in hypertension. The word “hypotension” is a typo and must be changed.

occurrences.original_stem: In a healthy heart, the QRS waves correspond to:
occurrences.explanation: The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization; atrial repolarization is usually hidden within it.

occurrences.original_stem: In first degree heart block what can be expected?

original_options.C: P wave is sometimes followed by QRS
original_options.D: P wave is not followed by QRS

occurrences.explanation: First-degree AV block has a prolonged PR interval, greater than 0.20 seconds, with each P wave followed by a QRS.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient has an elevated ST segment and inverted T wave, diagnosis?
occurrences.explanation: Acute MI can cause regional ST elevation and evolving T-wave inversion, but these findings require clinical and lead context and are not fully specific.

occurrences.original_stem: Patient presented with migratory polyarthritis and fever, their biopsy showed the following, what is it? PICTURE

original_options.A: Anitschkow cells characteristic in acute rheumatic heart disease
original_options.B: Plump plasma cells characteristic in rheumatic heart disease
original_options.C: Foreign body Giant cell characteristic in acute rheumatic heart disease
original_options.D: Aschoff cells characteristic in mitral valve prolapse

occurrences.explanation: The supplied histology shows an Aschoff body with Anitschkow macrophages, characteristic of rheumatic carditis. Foreign-body giant cells are not the correct characterization.

occurrences.original_stem: Which valve is most likely affected by this?
occurrences.explanation: The specimen shows a stenotic fish-mouth mitral orifice, a classic chronic rheumatic mitral valve appearance.

occurrences.original_stem: Which bacteria is most likely to cause infective endocarditis in IV drug users?
occurrences.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the most common pathogen in injection-drug-associated endocarditis, often involving the tricuspid valve.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with SLE has vegetations on his valves, what is the cause?
occurrences.explanation: Libman–Sacks endocarditis in SLE is a sterile immune-mediated valvular lesion associated with immune-complex injury.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is likely to spontaneously regress?
occurrences.explanation: Infantile (strawberry) hemangiomas commonly undergo spontaneous involution after an initial proliferative phase.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with von Hippel-Lindau disease has which of the following?
occurrences.explanation: VHL classically causes retinal/CNS hemangioblastomas (retinal capillary angiomas), not cavernous hemangioma. None of the listed choices accurately expresses the hallmark association.

occurrences.original_stem: Kaposi Sarcoma is caused by which of the following?
occurrences.explanation: Kaposi sarcoma is associated with human herpesvirus 8, also called Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus.

occurrences.original_stem: A female patient had gotten radiation and a mastectomy for her breast cancer, she is nowpresenting with ___? What is her current condition?
occurrences.explanation: Angiosarcoma can arise after radiation or in chronic lymphedema following mastectomy (Stewart–Treves syndrome).

occurrences.original_stem: What is true about coronary circulation?

original_options.A: The heart gets a rich blood supply from the right and left coronary arteries that arise from the coronary sinus
original_options.B: During ventricular systole the heart presses the arteries causing them to obstruct

occurrences.explanation: Systolic myocardial contraction compresses intramyocardial coronary vessels, particularly in the LV; most LV coronary perfusion occurs during diastole. Coronary arteries arise from aortic sinuses, not the coronary sinus.

occurrences.original_stem: A woman was shopping at a mall, suddenly she had chest pain with vasospasm. Immediately she used nitroglycerin and it relieved her symptoms. What is the mechanism of action of nitrates to alleviate chest pain? (not exact wording)
occurrences.explanation: Nitrates reduce myocardial oxygen demand mainly by venodilation and reduced preload; in vasospastic angina they also relieve coronary spasm, which is omitted from the choices.

occurrences.original_stem: Case about a patient of heat intolerance, weight loss, hyp_tension, ............ what do we test for?
occurrences.explanation: Heat intolerance and weight loss suggest hyperthyroidism, for which serum TSH is an initial test. The source stem and option B are incomplete.

occurrences.original_stem: Case: A 40 years old heavy smoker came to the hospital with long term hypertension 180/100, he has a cough and difficulty breathing, which medication is best to administer to control his BP?
occurrences.explanation: Both amlodipine and losartan can treat hypertension. Smoking, cough and breathlessness alone do not distinguish them; evaluate heart failure or lung disease and need for combination treatment.

occurrences.original_stem: How does low sodium help with treating hypertension?
occurrences.explanation: Lower sodium intake reduces sodium-associated extracellular fluid retention and can lower blood pressure.

occurrences.original_stem: A patient with MI showed a destruction of the cardiac muscle fibers. Which of the following cell junctions at intercalated disks and serve for keeping the integrity of the cardiac muscle during contraction are expected to be damaged in this condition?
occurrences.explanation: Macula adherens (desmosomes) prevents separation of cardiomyocytes during contraction. Fascia adherens also provides mechanical attachment; zonula occludens is not the correct intercalated-disc junction.

occurrences.original_stem: Second heart sound produced by closure of which valve? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: S2 results from aortic and pulmonary valve closure at the end of ventricular systole.

occurrences.original_stem: (Book Q.) A 3-year-old child is developing normally. Physical examination reveals a low-pitched cardiac murmur. An echocardiogram shows the presence of an ostium secundum, with a 1-cm defect. Which of the following abnormalities is most likely to be found in this child?
occurrences.explanation: An uncomplicated secundum ASD produces a left-to-right shunt because left atrial pressure exceeds right atrial pressure.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following mediators causes vasodilation?
occurrences.explanation: Endothelial nitric oxide relaxes vascular smooth muscle through soluble guanylyl cyclase and cGMP.

occurrences.original_stem: Second heart sound produced by closure of which valve? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: S2 is produced by closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is considered to be the first step in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis?
occurrences.explanation: Endothelial dysfunction is an initiating event in atherogenesis, permitting lipoprotein entry and inflammatory cell recruitment.

occurrences.original_stem: A 41-year old diabetic male has damaged vascular endothelium. Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) are present in this patient. Which of the following could result from such findings?
occurrences.explanation: AGE-related endothelial injury promotes a prothrombotic state and accelerated atherosclerosis. “Blood coagulopathy” is imprecise: rewrite as increased thrombosis tendency.

occurrences.original_stem: In a normal ECG, which of the following coincides with the absolute refractory period of a myocardial cell?

original_options.A: Start of Q to top of T wave

occurrences.explanation: The absolute refractory period extends from ventricular depolarization into much of repolarization, approximately QRS onset to around the T-wave peak; the remainder includes relative refractoriness.

occurrences.original_stem: [Incomplete source stem] segments from leads II, III, and avF. Which of the following is most likely seen in this patient?

original_options.A: Infarct in the inferior part of the heart with congestive heart failure
original_options.B: Infarct in the right part of the heart with hypotension
original_options.C: Infarct in the left part of the heart with bradycardia
original_options.D: Infarct in the inferior part of the heart with normal ventricular function

occurrences.explanation: The stem begins “.segments from leads II, III, and aVF. Which of the following is most likely seen in this patient?” Inferior lead changes may locate an inferior MI, but ventricular function, shock and right ventricular involvement cannot be inferred from the surviving fragment.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following heart sounds can be heard as a result of rapid blood filling from the atria into the ventricles (gushing)?
occurrences.explanation: Rapid ventricular filling can produce the third heart sound (S3), not S1. The only supplied option is wrong; add S3 as an option or convert to an ungraded explanation.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following primitive structures develops into the left auricle?
occurrences.explanation: The primitive atrium gives rise to the trabeculated parts and auricles of both atria.

occurrences.original_stem: Which structure can cause an atrial septal defect (ASD) through an opening?
occurrences.explanation: The foramen ovale is the intended atrial-level opening, but a patent foramen ovale is persistence of a flap communication and is anatomically distinct from a true tissue-deficiency ASD. Rewrite as “Which fetal atrial opening may remain patent after birth?”

occurrences.original_stem: [Incomplete source stem] hypotensive, with clammy and sweaty hands. Which of the following is most likely the type of shock?
occurrences.explanation: The surviving stem reads “.hypotensive, with clammy and sweaty hands. Which of the following is most likely the type of shock?” Hypovolemic and cardiogenic shock can both be cold and clammy; a cause such as bleeding is needed.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is contraindicated for initiating a beta blocker for congestive heart failure?
occurrences.explanation: Do not initiate or uptitrate a beta blocker during active decompensated heart failure; initiate after stabilization and adequate perfusion. Low EF is an indication for evidence-based beta blockade in stable HFrEF.

occurrences.original_stem: What are giant arteritis cells?
occurrences.explanation: Giant cell arteritis is a granulomatous vasculitis. If the question literally asks what giant cells are, they are fused macrophages (C). Rewrite to “What pattern of inflammation characterizes giant cell arteritis?” for answer D.

occurrences.original_stem: A woman presents to the clinic with a painful mass under her fingernail. Biopsy of the mass shows modified smooth muscle cells with stroma. What's the diagnosis?
occurrences.explanation: A painful subungual mass composed of modified smooth muscle cells is characteristic of a glomus tumor.

occurrences.original_stem: What is the most common heart condition that presents with an irregularly irregular rhythm? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: Atrial fibrillation characteristically produces an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm. Atrial flutter often has regular conduction unless the AV block varies.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is the most accurate description of Janeway lesions? (ECE)

original_options.A: Painful nodules in the pulp of fingers
original_options.B: Not painful spots on palms and soles of feet

occurrences.explanation: Janeway lesions are usually painless erythematous or hemorrhagic lesions on the palms and soles; painful fingertip/toe nodules are Osler nodes.

occurrences.original_stem: Smoking is an important element of social history. Which of the following is a consequence or complication of smoking? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: Smoking accelerates atherosclerosis and is a major modifiable risk factor for premature coronary artery disease.

occurrences.original_stem: Someone came with dyspnea, a cough that produces frothy sputum with wheezing. And heard with a stethoscope crackles, what is the diagnosis? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: Dyspnea, frothy sputum and crackles strongly suggest pulmonary edema; heart failure is a common underlying cause.

occurrences.original_stem: The correct position in a cardiovascular examination? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: A semirecumbent position around 45 degrees is customary for initial cardiovascular examination and jugular venous pressure assessment; specific maneuvers require repositioning.

occurrences.original_stem: A 25-year-old male patient has a past history of rheumatic fever. His auscultatory findings of the heart showed a loud first heart sound and a mid-diastolic murmur at apex. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: A loud S1 and mid-diastolic apical murmur after rheumatic fever indicate mitral stenosis. The only displayed answer, aortic regurgitation, is wrong.

occurrences.original_stem: Case with a patient that had splinter hemorrhage. Most likely diagnosis? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: Splinter hemorrhages can support infective endocarditis in the appropriate clinical setting, although they are not specific.

occurrences.original_stem: A 52-year old man develops sudden severe central chest pain after lifting heavy cases while moving to a new house. The pain radiates to the back and both shoulders but not to either arm. His BP is 170/110 mmHg, pulse rate is 92 beats per minute and the ECG is normal. He is distressed and sweaty, but not nauseated. What would you cinder the most likely diagnosis? (ECE)
occurrences.explanation: Sudden severe chest pain radiating to the back with marked hypertension suggests aortic dissection. A normal ECG does not exclude myocardial infarction.

occurrences.original_stem: How is the SA node rate affected by sympathetic stimulation?

original_options.D: increase slope of prepotential SA node

occurrences.explanation: Sympathetic beta-1 stimulation steepens SA-node phase 4 depolarization, so threshold is reached sooner and heart rate rises.

occurrences.original_stem: Which of the following is directly proportional to the rate of blood flow?
occurrences.explanation: Larger radius greatly increases flow: under Poiseuille assumptions flow is proportional to radius to the fourth power, and inversely proportional to length and viscosity. The stem should specify a positive relationship rather than direct linear proportionality.

occurrences.original_stem: A decrease in the slope of the prepotential SA node can be caused by?
occurrences.explanation: Vagal acetylcholine slows phase 4 depolarization and hyperpolarizes pacemaker cells, reducing SA-node firing.

occurrences.original_stem: What is the function of Atrio-Ventricular Bundle (AVB)?

original_options.A: Conducts impulses from SA node to ventricles
original_options.B: Conducts single from the apex to the rest of the ventricle

occurrences.explanation: The AV bundle conducts excitation from the AV node into the bundle branches and ventricular conduction system. Option A loosely describes the overall route; it should say AV node rather than SA node.

occurrences.original_stem: What primarily determines heart contractility?
occurrences.explanation: Intrinsic contractility depends on calcium handling and inotropic state at a given loading condition; preload influences stroke volume through Frank–Starling. Neither HR nor preload is an adequate single answer to this wording.

occurrences.original_stem: vascular system developed at :
occurrences.explanation: Cardiovascular development begins during the third embryonic week.

occurrences.original_stem: ostium secundum is a defect in:
occurrences.explanation: The ostium secundum normally develops in the upper septum primum by programmed resorption. A secundum ASD may result from excessive primum resorption or inadequate secundum development. Clarify whether the question asks the normal opening or the defect.

occurrences.original_stem: A newly born baby is born cyanotic & having difficulty of breathing , on examination a well-heard diastolic murmur suggested valvular stenosis , the imaging technique used is :
occurrences.explanation: Echocardiography is the first-line imaging test for suspected congenital structural or valvular heart disease.

occurrences.original_stem: Between AV valve closure and opening of semilunar valve is the following phase:
occurrences.explanation: The period after AV valve closure and before semilunar valve opening is ventricular isovolumetric (isometric) contraction.

occurrences.original_stem: the graph shows ventricle pressure-volume relationship; point A is: (no graph was given)
occurrences.explanation: No pressure-volume graph is supplied, so the meaning of point A cannot be determined from the label alone.

occurrences.original_stem: The lowest ventricular volume occurs during which phase:
occurrences.explanation: End-systolic volume is maintained throughout isovolumetric relaxation. Volume reaches this minimum at the end of reduced ejection, but A is the best phase among the supplied choices.
